newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca shares rebound after recent battering.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca shares rebound after recent battering.

text.p: Drugs group Zeneca Plc saw its shares rebound on Tuesday from last week's battering, but analysts said the move was merely a correction and reported no resurgence of bid rumours in the marketplace.
Zeneca hit a high of 16.40 stg per share earlier, but has since slipped slightly to 16.37 1/2 stg, up 36 pence.
Nigel Barnes, analyst at Merrill Lynch, said: "It's nothing special. The stock was hit on Friday and it's just bounced back through the 16.00 (stg) support level."
He said he was unaware of any bid rumours re-emerging in the marketplace.
Another analyst said: "Zeneca has fallen quite a bit lately," pointing to the dampening effect of a strong pound on overseas business and the latest round of bid speculation fading away.
She added that it remained a highly volatile stock. "It can go up thirty or forty pence a day and then drop back the next day. But fundamentally we favour the stock."
